findings.title: A dry run records the qodo-gate status as posted though it was only rehearsed
findings.why: gate() sets s.gateShown = key and saves it after write(), which in QODO_DRY_RUN only logs. That is Rule 7's #60 pattern: a rehearsal saved as posted. A dry run must use a copy of the state (QODO_STATE), so the live runner isn't affected. But a rehearsal that is run twice on the same copy skips the post the second time and doesn't show the write it would make.

findings.title: A moved head gets a red qodo-gate on a commit the runner never checked
findings.why: When prHead differs from s.head, the runner posts failure on prHead ('the commit the runner pushed and Qodo reviewed'), even if Qodo finished a clean review of prHead. It can overwrite a correct success that the owner posted with `qodo-gate.mjs <PR> --post`, which blocks a mergeable PR until the owner posts again. The PR description says a moved head is a failure, so this is the intended design. The cost is a red status that doesn't describe that commit.

findings.title: An unreadable Qodo review exits 2, the code for 'no finished review yet'
findings.why: gateVerdict maps readError to 'wait', so a missing qodo binary or failed read gives a pending status and exit 2. A script calling the CLI can't tell 'Qodo is still reviewing' from 'the gate can't run'. It still fails closed: pending blocks the merge.

findings.title: The 140-character cut can split an emoji or other surrogate pair
findings.why: shown.slice(0, 139) cuts UTF-16 code units, so a description from a read error or finding text that has a non-BMP character at position 139 ends in a lone surrogate. The status description is then malformed.
